title: introduce-cost-playbook-assembler-and-prefill-presets
author: Lina Ortega
description: Motivation: Provide a composable, testable 'Cost Playbook' construct that bundles batching defaults, cache/prefill policies, and quantization profile recommendations into tenant-scoped artifacts that can be dry-run against workload traces and rolled out with safety gates. This PR implements the playbook assembler service, a CLI to generate/dry-run playbooks, a small policy language for combining batch/cache/quant hints, telemetry hooks for unit-econ evaluation, and migration logic to convert existing tenant defaults into playbook form. Key goals: reduce manual config drift, make autosuggest rules reproducible, and enable canary rollouts that automatically revert on quality or latency regressions. Highlights: implemented playbook assembler (internal API + controller), added costctl playbook subcommands (generate/dryrun/validate/apply), introduced a compact playbook JSON schema and a playbook catalog under tenant defaults, wiring to the prefiller and batcher to accept playbook hints (batch window, max_microbatch_size, prefill_budget_pct), integrated quant profile suggestions with safety thresholds (quality_delta_allowed=0.02), telemetry events (playbook.evaluation.start/finish, playbook.rollback.trigger), and end-to-end CI checks including dry-run simulation against 3 representative traces. Testing & rollout: unit tests for assembler, integration tests running dry-run traces in CI; local e2e playbook apply validated against a synthetic tenant in prefiller sandbox; staged rollout plan: alpha tenants -> canary pool (5 tenants) with latency SLO watch -> ramp to all tenants over 48h. Backwards compatibility: existing tenant defaults are migrated automatically to a single implicit playbook; users can opt out by setting tenant.playbook_mode=legacy. Migration includes a safe snapshot export and a rollback path. Security & privacy: no change to PII handling; playbook artifacts stored encrypted at rest. See docs update for cost playbooks and CLI usage. Checklist: [x] implement assembler core; [x] add playbook catalog UI endpoints; [x] add costctl subcommands; [x] add telemetry hooks; [x] add integration tests; [x] add migration tool; [x] docs and changelog updated. Related: references ENG-4021 (economy playbooks design), ENG-4109 (prefill policy consolidation).

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Overall this looks good but we need a hard SLO hook in the controller to avoid cascading regresses; can you add a configured latency threshold and immediate rollback?
Lina Ortega: Added playbook.rollback.trigger telemetry and a controller-level threshold (config.playbook.latency_slo_pct=1.2) with immediate rollback action. Updated tests to cover rollback flow.
Marta Nowak: Suggest tightening default quality_delta_allowed to 0.015 for chat workloads; also add a note in docs about non-deterministic quant effects.
Lina Ortega: Reduced default to 0.015 for chat workload class and documented stochastic quant impacts. Left an escape hatch per-tenant.
Ethan Rios: CI flaky on dryrun against trace_latin intermittently; can we assert deterministic seeds in simulator?
Lina Ortega: Fixed simulator seed in tests and added a rerun step in CI config for flaky simulation jobs.

release_notes: Added 'Cost Playbooks' framework: playbook assembler service, tenant playbook catalog, costctl playbook commands, safe migration path from tenant defaults, telemetry for evaluation and rollback, and guidance for canary rollouts and latency/quality safety gates. This enables automated, reproducible batch/cache/quant recommendations and dry-run simulations before applying changes to production tenants.
